questions.q: In which year was the first non-synchronous Census conducted in India?
questions.why: The first ever census in India was conducted non-synchronously in 1872 under the viceroyalty of Lord Mayo.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India when the first synchronous (complete) Census was conducted in 1881?
questions.why: Lord Ripon initiated the first synchronous decadal census in 1881, standardizing the 10-year cycle.

questions.q: Which year is famously known as the 'Year of Great Divide' in the demographic history of India?
questions.why: The 1921 Census was the only time India recorded a negative decadal growth rate (-0.31%) due to famines and the Spanish flu.

questions.q: Under which Ministry is the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner functioning?
questions.why: The Ministry of Home Affairs is the nodal ministry responsible for conducting the decadal census.

questions.q: Under which Schedule of the Indian Constitution is the 'Census' listed?
questions.why: Census is listed under Entry 69 of the Union List in the 7th Schedule, making it exclusively a central government subject.

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution grants the Parliament the exclusive power to legislate on the Census?
questions.why: Article 246 gives the Union Parliament exclusive power to make laws regarding subjects in the Union List, including the Census.

questions.q: The legal framework for conducting the census is provided by the Census Act, which was passed in:
questions.why: The Census Act of 1948, pioneered by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, provides the permanent legal framework for the census.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Demography'?
questions.why: Henry Walter conducted the first known local population census in Dacca in 1830, earning him this title.

questions.q: Who was the first Census Commissioner of India during the 1881 Census?
questions.why: W.C. Plowden served as the first Census Commissioner of India for the 1881 synchronous census.

questions.q: In which year did India launch its first National Family Planning Programme?
questions.why: India was the first country in the world to launch a state-sponsored family planning programme in 1952.

questions.q: According to Census 2011, what is the total population of India?
questions.why: The exact official figure for the 2011 Census was 1,210,854,977 (approx. 1.21 billion).

questions.q: What percentage of the total world population did India represent according to the 2011 Census?
questions.why: In 2011, India accounted for 17.5% of the global population while occupying only 2.4% of the world's land area.

questions.q: What was the decadal population growth rate of India during 2001-2011?
questions.why: The population grew by 17.64% over the decade, showing a sharp decline from the 21.54% growth rate of the previous decade.

questions.q: According to Census 2011, what is the overall literacy rate of India?
questions.why: The overall literacy rate was 74.04%, with significant disparities between male and female literacy.

questions.q: What is the male literacy rate in India as per the 2011 Census?
questions.why: Male literacy stood at 82.14%, highlighting a persistent gender gap in education.

questions.q: What is the female literacy rate in India as per the 2011 Census?
questions.why: Female literacy was recorded at 65.46%, which was an improvement from 2001 but still 16.68% behind males.

questions.q: What was the overall Sex Ratio of India in the 2011 Census?
questions.why: The final data for the 2011 Census reported a sex ratio of 943 females per 1000 males (up from 933 in 2001).

questions.q: What was the Child Sex Ratio (0-6 years) in India according to Census 2011?
questions.why: The final child sex ratio was 919 (provisional was 914), showing a concerning decline from 927 in 2001.

questions.q: Which Indian state has the highest population density as per Census 2011?
questions.why: Bihar recorded the highest population density with 1,106 persons per square kilometer.

questions.q: Which Indian state has the lowest population density as per Census 2011?
questions.why: Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest density with only 17 persons per square kilometer.

questions.q: Which state holds the highest population in India according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state, housing nearly 16.5% of India's total population.

questions.q: Which is the least populated state in India according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Sikkim is the least populated state, with a total population of just over 6 lakh people.

questions.q: Which state recorded a negative decadal population growth rate in the 2011 Census?
questions.why: Nagaland was the only state to record a negative growth rate of -0.58% during the 2001-2011 decade.

questions.q: Which state boasts the highest sex ratio according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Kerala has the highest sex ratio with 1,084 females per 1,000 males.

questions.q: Among the Indian states, which has the lowest sex ratio according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Haryana recorded the lowest sex ratio among states with only 879 females per 1,000 males.

questions.q: Which state has the lowest literacy rate according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Bihar recorded the lowest overall literacy rate at 61.8%.

questions.q: Which Union Territory has the highest population based on Census 2011?
questions.why: The NCT of Delhi is the most populous Union Territory by a massive margin.

questions.q: Which Union Territory has the least population based on Census 2011?
questions.why: Lakshadweep is the least populated UT, with roughly 64,000 residents.

questions.q: Which Union Territory recorded the highest sex ratio in Census 2011?
questions.why: Puducherry recorded the highest sex ratio among UTs with 1,037 females per 1,000 males.

questions.q: Which Union Territory recorded the highest literacy rate in Census 2011?
questions.why: Lakshadweep has the highest literacy rate among UTs at 91.85%.

questions.q: What is the overall population density of India as per Census 2011?
questions.why: The national average population density increased from 325 in 2001 to 382 persons per sq km in 2011.

questions.q: What percentage of India's population lived in urban areas according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Exactly 31.16% of the population lived in urban areas, while 68.84% resided in rural areas.

questions.q: Which state has the maximum percentage of urban population?
questions.why: In terms of percentage, Goa is the most urbanized state (62.2%). Maharashtra has the highest absolute urban numbers.

questions.q: Which state has the maximum percentage of rural population?
questions.why: Himachal Pradesh is the least urbanized state, with exactly 89.97% of its population living in rural areas.

questions.q: Which state has the highest percentage of Scheduled Caste (SC) population?
questions.why: By percentage, Punjab has the highest SC population (31.9%). UP has the highest absolute number of SCs.

questions.q: Which state has the largest absolute number of Scheduled Tribes (ST)?
questions.why: Madhya Pradesh houses the largest tribal population in terms of sheer numbers.

questions.q: What was the mascot of the 2011 Census of India?
questions.why: A female enumerator was chosen as the mascot to honor the primary data collectors on the ground.

questions.q: What was the official slogan of the 2011 Census?
questions.why: The theme highlighted that the data collected dictates the future planning of the nation.

questions.q: Which is the most populous district in India according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Thane in Maharashtra was the most populous district in 2011, though it was later bifurcated.

questions.q: Which was the least populous district in India according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Dibang Valley in Arunachal Pradesh is the least populous district.

questions.q: Which Indian state recorded the highest decadal population growth rate (2001-2011)?
questions.why: Meghalaya recorded a massive decadal growth rate of 27.9%.

questions.q: Which linguistic group is the second most spoken in India after Hindi?
questions.why: Bengali is the second most spoken language, representing about 8.03% of the population.

questions.q: What percentage of India's population is constituted by Scheduled Tribes (ST) as per 2011?
questions.why: Scheduled Tribes constitute 8.6%, while Scheduled Castes constitute 16.6% of the total population.

questions.q: Which religious community witnessed the highest decadal growth rate in the 2011 Census?
questions.why: The Muslim population recorded the highest decadal growth rate at 24.6%.

questions.q: Across how many districts was the Census 2011 conducted?
questions.why: The 2011 census covered 640 districts across all states and union territories.

questions.q: The delayed Population Census is now officially projected to be completed in which year?
questions.why: Due to massive delays caused by the pandemic, the completion target is officially set for 2027.

questions.q: For the first time since 1931, the upcoming 2027 Census will include which specific enumeration?
questions.why: The government has indicated that a detailed counting of Other Backward Classes (OBCs) will be included.

questions.q: The upcoming 2027 Census will be a landmark event as it will be India's first ever:
questions.why: Data will be collected entirely using mobile applications, moving away from pen-and-paper.

questions.q: The data from the 2027 Census is expected to be the crucial baseline for which major constitutional exercise?
questions.why: The freeze on redrawing Lok Sabha boundaries ends after 2026, making the 2027 data essential for delimitation.

questions.q: According to UN and Worldometer projections, what is the estimated population of India in 2026?
questions.why: Demographic projections place India's population around 1.47 billion for the year 2026.

questions.q: Which innovative citizen feature is being introduced for the 2027 Digital Census?
questions.why: Citizens will have the option to fill in their own census details online through a secure portal.

questions.q: The upcoming 2027 Census will be which edition of the continuous decadal census in India?
questions.why: It will be the 16th overall census since 1872, and the 8th since independence.

questions.q: Alongside the house listing phase of the 2027 Census, which other major database will be updated?
questions.why: The NPR, which lists 'usual residents', is traditionally updated during the house listing phase of the census.

questions.q: In how many languages will the mobile app for the 2027 Digital Census be available?
questions.why: The digital data collection app is designed to support 16 different languages.

questions.q: Based on 2026-2027 demographic projections, what is the expected median age of the Indian population?
questions.why: India is aging slightly, with the median age projected to reach 29.2 years by 2026.

questions.q: According to 2026 projections, roughly what percentage of India's population will be living in urban areas?
questions.why: Urbanization is steadily increasing, with projections showing 37.6% urban population by 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following constitutional amendments currently freezes the total number of Lok Sabha seats until the first census after 2026?
questions.why: The 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze on Lok Sabha seats until the first census post-2026.

questions.q: Which state is projected to remain the most populous state in the 2027 Census?
questions.why: Current growth trajectories guarantee that UP will comfortably retain its top spot.

questions.q: The 2011 SECC (Socio-Economic and Caste Census) was conducted by the MHA alongside which other Ministry?
questions.why: Unlike the regular census, the 2011 SECC was jointly executed by the Ministry of Rural Development and the MHA.

questions.q: What was the primary reason cited for the unprecedented delay of the 16th Indian Census?
questions.why: The exercise scheduled for 2021 was infinitely delayed due to global COVID-19 lockdowns and administrative backlogs.

questions.q: The upcoming Census 2027 will be the first in India's history to feature which major technological shift?
questions.why: Census 2027 is India's first digital census, utilizing mobile apps and a self-enumeration portal to eliminate traditional paper-based data collection.

questions.q: During which phase of Census 2027 has the government officially approved the comprehensive enumeration of Castes?
questions.why: The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs recently decided that a comprehensive caste enumeration will take place during Phase II in February 2027.

questions.q: How many languages will be supported on the new citizen Self-Enumeration Portal for Census 2027?
questions.why: The dedicated online portal allows citizens to independently fill their household details in 16 different regional languages prior to field visits.

questions.q: What is the official standard 'Reference Date' set for the Population Enumeration phase of Census 2027 across most of India?
questions.why: The official 'Census Moment' or reference date for Census 2027 is fixed at 00:00 hours of March 1, 2027 for most states.

questions.q: As per recent demographic projections for 2026, what is the estimated median age of the Indian population?
questions.why: India remains a young nation with a projected median age of 29.2 years in 2026, driving the nation's ongoing demographic dividend.

questions.q: According to a recent exam, what was the exact overall literacy rate of India at the time of the first post-independence census in 1951?
questions.why: At the dawn of the republic in 1951, India's overall literacy rate was a mere 18.33%, reflecting massive post-colonial educational challenges.

questions.q: According to Census 2011, which Indian state has the highest difference between male and female literacy rates?
questions.why: Rajasthan recorded the highest gender gap in literacy in 2011, with male literacy at 79.2% and female literacy lagging at just 52.1%.

questions.q: As per demographic projections for the 2026-2027 cycle, what is India's approximate Total Fertility Rate (TFR)?
questions.why: India's TFR has officially fallen to 1.9, which is below the replacement level of 2.1, indicating a long-term stabilization of population growth.

questions.q: During the Houselisting phase (Phase 1) of Census 2027, which other major national database will simultaneously be updated?
questions.why: The NPR, a register of all 'usual residents' of the country, is systematically updated alongside the house listing phase of the decadal census.

questions.q: According to a recent PYQ, which Northeastern state recorded the highest population in Census 2011?
questions.why: With a population of over 3.12 crore in 2011, Assam easily remains the most populous state in the entire Northeastern region.

questions.q: The Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) launched for 2027 primarily serves what purpose?
questions.why: The CMMS portal is a near real-time monitoring dashboard for officers to track field performance and enumeration progress instantly.

questions.q: What is the projected percentage of India's population living in urban areas by 2026-2027?
questions.why: Driven by rapid internal migration to major metro areas, India's urban population share is projected to rise to approximately 37.6% by 2026.

questions.q: For snow-bound and non-synchronous areas like Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh, what is the reference date for Census 2027?
questions.why: Due to harsh winter conditions, snow-bound areas are enumerated earlier, with their specific reference date set to October 1, 2026.

questions.q: As per the 2011 Census of India, which state had the lowest child sex ratio (0-6 years)?
questions.why: Haryana recorded a concerningly low child sex ratio of just 834 females per 1,000 males, the lowest among all Indian states in 2011.

questions.q: Census 2027 marks which specific edition of the continuous decadal census in India since independence?
questions.why: While it is the 16th overall census since 1872, Census 2027 specifically marks the 8th demographic enumeration since India gained independence.

questions.q: According to Census 2011, which state has the highest percentage of Scheduled Tribe (ST) population to its total population?
questions.why: While MP has the highest absolute ST population, Mizoram leads by percentage with roughly 94.4% tribal population.

questions.q: As per the 2011 Census, which state recorded the second highest literacy rate in India?
questions.why: Kerala ranks first (94%), and Mizoram closely follows as the second most literate state with 91.3% literacy.

questions.q: What was the rural population percentage of India as per the Census 2011?
questions.why: While 31.16% of India is urbanized, the vast majority (68.84%) still resides in rural areas according to 2011 data.

questions.q: According to Census 2011, which Union Territory has the lowest sex ratio?
questions.why: Daman and Diu recorded the lowest sex ratio among UTs with only 618 females per 1,000 males.

questions.q: Which state has the highest number of 'Metropolitan Cities' (million-plus population) according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Uttar Pradesh and Kerala both have 7 million-plus cities, the highest among Indian states in the 2011 data.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, which state has the highest percentage of 'Scheduled Caste' population?
questions.why: Punjab has the highest SC population by percentage (31.9%), whereas UP has the highest SC population by absolute numbers.

questions.q: The 2027 Digital Census will use which specific method to ensure data security and prevent duplication?
questions.why: The upcoming digital census plans to use Aadhaar-seeded validation to ensure the integrity of self-enumeration data and prevent double counting.

questions.q: According to 2011 Census data, which state has the lowest female literacy rate?
questions.why: Bihar has the lowest female literacy rate at 51.5%, followed closely by Rajasthan at 52.1%.

questions.q: What is the density of population in Delhi (NCT) according to Census 2011?
questions.why: Delhi is the most densely populated UT/State in India, with 11,320 persons per square kilometer as of 2011.

questions.q: Which was the first district in India to be fully 'Census-mapped' using GIS technology for the 2027 cycle?
questions.why: Gandhinagar was a pilot district for advanced GIS mapping to ensure every household is digitally geotagged for the upcoming census.

questions.q: According to Census 2011, what is the work participation rate of females in India?
questions.why: The female work participation rate was recorded at 25.5%, showing a significant gap compared to the male rate of 53.3%.

questions.q: Which religious group recorded the highest literacy rate in India as per Census 2011?
questions.why: Jains are the most literate religious community in India, with an overall literacy rate of approximately 94.1%.

questions.q: The upcoming 2027 Census will be conducted under which constitutional provision?
questions.why: Article 246 places the Census in the Union List (Entry 69), giving the Central Government exclusive authority to conduct it.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, how many 'Statutory Towns' were there in India?
questions.why: There were 4,041 statutory towns and 3,892 census towns, making a total of 7,935 towns in 2011.

questions.q: What is the estimated 'Demographic Dividend' window for India projected to end based on current census trends?
questions.why: India's demographic dividend (working-age population bulk) is projected to peak around 2041 and last until approximately 2055-56.
